channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi oil refinery as Iran war widens to Red Sea
item.dc:creator: Mohamad El Chamaa
item.description: The strikes by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels could add to the pressure on global oil markets on top of disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Trump swings back toward diplomacy in escalating war with Iran
item.dc:creator: Michael Birnbaum
item.description: After threatening a “massive attack,” the president said his envoys were talking with Tehran but left open the possibility of a sharp military escalation.

item.title: Mali’s government does not rule out U.S. military intervention
item.dc:creator: Rachel Chason, John Hudson
item.description: The country’s foreign minister said, however, that anyone wishing to partner with the West African nation “must respect” its sovereignty.

item.title: Why Japan wants to create its first modern spy agency since World War II
item.dc:creator: Michelle Lee, Chie Tanaka, Greg Miller
item.description: President Donald Trump’s push for Japanese self-reliance aligns with the long-standing desire of conservatives in Tokyo to build intelligence capabilities.

item.title: House votes to limit Trump on Iran; Senate fails to advance similar measure
item.dc:creator: Noah Robertson, Mariana Alfaro, Theodoric Meyer
item.description: The votes marked the first test of Republican support for the conflict since President Donald Trump resumed military strikes against Tehran this month.
